content.title: Falling Glass Elevator | Constricted Descent to Action Escape
content.summary: An adult engineer escapes a damaged ice-refinery lift into a snow yard. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One carrier, one descent direction and one adult occupant remain continuous. + Every impact leaves persistent physical damage inside the enclosure. + The interior view confirms the same carrier state established outside. + Open-space evidence appears before the exit becomes available. + One terminal threshold releases the occupant while preserving the damaged origin behind.
quick_start.recommended_input: Track one transparent mining lift descending the outside of an original ice refinery with one adult engineer inside. Inside the same cage, reconnect the engineer on one knee among ice fragments as she stands and checks the door. Open the door once at the base; the engineer exits into the open snow yard and the damaged lift remains behind her.
required_anchors: One carrier, one descent direction and one adult occupant remain continuous.
Every impact leaves persistent physical damage inside the enclosure.
Open-space evidence appears before the exit becomes available.
One terminal threshold releases the occupant while preserving the damaged origin behind.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: An adult engineer escapes a damaged ice-refinery lift into a snow yard. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

invariants.rule: One carrier, one descent direction and one adult occupant remain continuous.
invariants.purpose: Establishes the baseline identity, object or geography that every later state must preserve.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact baseline rule, later changes cannot be attributed to the same subject, object or place, so the sequence loses its reference state. Removed rule: "One carrier, one descent direction and one adult occupant remain continuous."

invariants.rule: Every impact leaves persistent physical damage inside the enclosure.
invariants.purpose: Makes the visible trigger precede and explain the first mechanism response.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact trigger rule, the response appears spontaneously and the central cause-and-effect claim is no longer demonstrated. Removed rule: "Every impact leaves persistent physical damage inside the enclosure."

invariants.rule: The interior view confirms the same carrier state established outside.
invariants.purpose: Keeps the middle progression registered instead of allowing an unexplained reset.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact progression rule, the middle can jump to a replacement state and the accumulated result is no longer traceable. Removed rule: "The interior view confirms the same carrier state established outside."

invariants.rule: Open-space evidence appears before the exit becomes available.
invariants.purpose: Reconnects the changed or partial state to the established subject and spatial anchor.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact reconnection rule, detail or transformed shots can belong to a different subject or geography and continuity cannot be verified. Removed rule: "Open-space evidence appears before the exit becomes available."

invariants.rule: One terminal threshold releases the occupant while preserving the damaged origin behind.
invariants.purpose: Turns the terminal hold into observable proof that the mechanism completed.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without this exact terminal-proof rule, the sequence stops on motion alone and never confirms the promised outcome or preserved aftermath. Removed rule: "One terminal threshold releases the occupant while preserving the damaged origin behind."
